Cross-validate a fit

Source: R/crossval.R
crossval.Rd

Splits the observed cells at random into folds groups. Each group is held out in turn: the model is refitted to the other cells, with the fit's formula, covariates, priors, nugget and sampler settings, and then predicts the held-out cells. Use it to check calibration out of sample and to compare models fitted to the same cells. The same seed gives the same folds, so models are compared on the same splits. The mean log score is higher for the better model; about 5% of observations should fall outside their 95% predictive interval.

Usage

crossval(
  fit,
  folds = 10,
  fold = NULL,
  control = fit$control,
  checkpoint_dir = NULL,
  seed = 1
)

Arguments

fit

A fit_areal() object.

folds

The number of folds, assigned at random; or a fold label for each observed cell, in the order of fit$data$cells, for folds of your own: by site, by country (spatial cross-validation, which tests extrapolation to unsurveyed places), or by period.

fold

Which folds to run (default all), as numbers or labels, e.g. to run them in separate sessions.

control

Sampler settings for the refits: mcmc_control() or a list of some of its arguments (default: the fit's).

checkpoint_dir

A folder for the refits' checkpoints: fold k of K with split seed s checkpoints in <checkpoint_dir>/cv_seed<s>_fold_<k>_of_<K>. NULL: none.

seed

Seed of the random split into folds.

Value

An object of class stareal_cv:

cells

one row per held-out cell: fold, cell_id, id, t, time, y, k, obs_prev (100 y / k), pred_mean, pred_lo, pred_hi (mean and 95% interval of the cell's prevalence, with the nugget), rep_lo, rep_hi (95% posterior-predictive interval of 100 y / k); all prevalences in percent; pit (randomised probability integral transform of y), outside (pit outside 0.025-0.975), and log_score, the log predictive density of y

folds

one row per fold, and overall: the number held out, RMSE of pred_mean against obs_prev (percentage points), percent outside the 95% interval, mean log score and correlation

fold_of

the fold of every observed cell

Compare models with compare_cv().

Details

Held-out cells are predicted as observations, with the cell nugget, so pred_* describe the prevalence a new survey of the cell would see, not the smoother surface of predict().

Each fold is a full refit, so this costs folds (or length(fold)) times the fit.

Examples

# \donttest{
fr <- areal_lattice(4, 4)
tf <- time_frame(n_steps = 5)
sim <- simulate_areal(fr, tf, n_cells = 40, seed = 1)
fit <- fit_areal(sim, control = list(n_iter = 100, n_burn = 50, n_store = 25, n_chains = 1,
                                     ess_sweeps = 2, verbose = FALSE))
cv <- crossval(fit, folds = 4)
cv
#> <stareal_cv> 4-fold cross-validation (seed 1), 4 folds run, 40 cells held out
#>   RMSE 13.75 points; 2.5% outside the 95% predictive interval; mean log score -3.254; correlation 0.51
# }
